headline: Launch Your Side Project Without Spending a Week Writing Copy
summary: Learn how to streamline your product launch copy across multiple platforms, saving you time and energy.
details: Launching a side project can be as time-consuming as building it, especially when it comes to crafting effective copy for various platforms. This guide provides a step-by-step playbook to help founders efficiently create compelling content for Product Hunt, Reddit, Twitter, newsletters, and more.

The first crucial step is to identify your product's unique selling proposition (USP). All launch copy should directly support this core message. Understanding what sets your product apart from competitors allows for honest positioning and preemptive addressing of potential objections.

Thorough competitor research is key. Analyze their Product Hunt descriptions, Reddit posts, and other online presence to identify gaps in their messaging and successful strategies. This insight helps you tailor your own copy to fill those voids and avoid common pitfalls.

A successful launch requires a multi-faceted content strategy. This includes tailored descriptions for Product Hunt, platform-specific Reddit posts, engaging Twitter threads, personalized newsletter pitches, and SEO-optimized landing page copy.

Manual submission to numerous directories and platforms can take 20-30 hours. Tools like welaunch.sh can automate competitor analysis and even simulate potential skeptical comments, preparing you for launch day challenges.

Different platforms demand different tones and formats. Product Hunt readers appreciate authenticity and bullet points, while Reddit users are highly sensitive to marketing speak. Adapting your message to each audience is vital for engagement.

headline_marked: Mobileye [[launches US robotaxi service]] with 100 autonomous vehicles by 2027
headline: Mobileye launches US robotaxi service with 100 autonomous vehicles by 2027
summary: The self-driving tech supplier plans to scale to 17,000 robotaxis within five years of its initial US city launch in 2027.
details: Mobileye, an Intel subsidiary, is expanding beyond its role as a supplier to enter the US robotaxi market directly. The company announced plans to launch its own autonomous vehicle service in an unnamed US city, starting in 2027 with an initial fleet of 100 vehicles.

The company aims to significantly scale its robotaxi operations, projecting a fleet of approximately 17,000 autonomous vehicles within five years of the service's launch. This move positions Mobileye to compete directly in the burgeoning robotaxi industry.

Mobileye's CEO, Amnon Shashua, stated that the robotaxi revolution is just beginning and has immense potential to transform travel. He noted the industry's increasing reliance on a few key technology providers and business models.

Previously known for supplying computer vision chips for driver assistance systems, Mobileye has developed its own chips and software for autonomous driving. The company currently supplies its self-driving system to automakers like Volkswagen.

To manage its new venture, Mobileye will establish a dedicated operating business. The service will leverage Moovit, the transit and ride-hailing app owned by Mobileye, for its consumer-facing operations, while the fleet management will be handled internally.

Mobileye emphasizes that this new service will complement its existing supplier business, not replace it. The company plans to work with "AV-ready vehicle platform manufacturers" but has not yet named the specific vehicle model for its fleet, though illustrations suggest a modified electric crossover.
